chapter: Mingus and the call from Hampton
title: Hampton's band when Wes was in it, with two bassists
summary: Monk lists players in the band and recalls Mingus and Charlie Harris as two bassists; he himself was top bassist in Indianapolis.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: He had a lot of good people in his bands.
He had some giants in his bands.
Well, when Wes was in the band, who was in it?

That was the bunch with Al Gray and Johnny Board and I can't think of all those guys' names, was in the band when Wes was there. Ah, Benny Powell, Earl Walker...Earl Fox Walker. I can't think of all the players that were in the band. But I do remember these two: Charlie Mingus was in the band, in Lionel Hampton's band...
I've seen a picture of that band, yeah, with the two bass players.
Right. That's the first time I saw anything like that. And now I'm into bass myself for a couple of years, right?

Upright, oh yeah. Electric hadn't come out. So I'm like top gun around Indianapolis, but that's not saying a whole lot because there weren't a whole lot of guys around there. I could just about pick my jobs almost, by now. But...I was playing good. And I'm not, I don't mean to be vain with you. I'm not saying I was no kind of superstar or whatever, but I was at the height of my potential, I knew that, and I was playing good.
